subject: Mathematics
overall_notes: Strong pair on B2.8 (numerator as repeated addition) with clear bridges to Lesson 3 (repeated addition IS multiplication) and forward to mixed-number territory. Trap is the unit-fraction-collapse error (3 × 1/4 = 3) — a real, research-aligned Grade-3 misconception with concrete strip-based recovery and a branching long-term plan. Materials are everyday (fraction strips, anchor chart, sticky notes) with the puppet explicitly OPTIONAL and a clear voice/two-stuffed-animal alternative — runnable on any day. Tony's voice anchors minds_on, action discussion, and consolidation; success criteria are 'I can'; vocabulary defined child-friendly. Worksheet's three parts each map to a named success criterion AND deliberately vary the format (Part 1 fraction→decomposition, Part 2 multiplication→fraction with whole-number identification — a transfer twist, Part 3 open three-ways generation). Math authenticity is strong: children invent/compare strategies for when N × 1/D yields a whole number (N is a multiple of D), and the misconception is named in the precise conceptual frame (unit-as-counted-quantity).
